clue.text: Work in intricate lace re-fleeted skill of Queen

indicators.note: in tells us one piece goes inside the other
something intricate is tangled, so the letters of the following word are worked into a new order

parts.note: op is the usual short form of opus, a musical work

indicators.note: reflected, as in a mirror, means the word for skill is read backwards

parts.note: art means skill, as in the art of persuasion

explanation.surface: A lacemaker's elaborate work mirrors a royal's handiwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intricate' rearranges LACE to CLEA, and OP goes in after CLE; 're-flected' turns ART into TRA. The printed 're-fleeted' is an OCR slip for the line-broken 're-flected'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleopatra was the last ruling monarch of Ptolemaic Egypt.

clue.text: Letter C in dish which everybody uses

indicators.note: in places the letters inside the dish

parts.note: a curry is a spiced dish
en is the spelt-out name of the letter N

explanation.surface: A recipe note about putting the letter C into a meal everyone eats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter C' looks like one item but gives two: EN, the name of the letter N, then C; both go inside CURRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Money in circulation is the medium of exchange that all members of a country use.

clue.text: Not all the victors displace people from their homes

indicators.note: Not all says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Conquerors do not all turn people out of their homes.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn tenants out by legal process is exactly to throw occupants out of a dwelling.

clue.text: Star engine's part, mostly, could be in hauling this?

definitions.text: Star engine's part, mostly, could be in hauling this?

indicators.note: could be invites the solver to see what the following letters might become once rearranged

parts.note: the possessive s counts here as a letter of the fodder

indicators.note: mostly means the word part loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A thought about which carriages a star locomotive might pull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims PART to PAR; 'could be' then rearranges STAR, ENGINES and PAR together. The whole clue also describes what a star engine hauls.
explanation.definitionFit: A locomotive pulls a line of coaches carrying travellers.

clue.text: Sets are made up in a small block

indicators.note: made up signals the letters of the previous words are assembled into something new

explanation.surface: Sets are assembled within a small block.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made up' rearranges SETS ARE.
explanation.definitionFit: A tessera is one of the small square tiles used in mosaic.

clue.text: Cunning one in charge of old

parts.note: arch means sly or knowing, as in an arch look
a means one, as in a dozen

explanation.surface: A crafty person running things from long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic describes something belonging to an earlier age, ancient or antiquated.

clue.text: River islands?

parts.note: IS is the abbreviation for island; the plural gives two of them
the second abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A geography quiz asking about river islands.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural 'islands' supplies two IS abbreviations. The Isis is the name of the Thames as it flows through Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: The Thames at Oxford is traditionally called by this name.

clue.text: At the pig's cooking you could eat it

indicators.note: cooking, as in cooking the books, means the letters before it are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A farmhouse remark: the pig's dinner is cooking and you could eat it too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooking' rearranges ATTHEPIGS, the letters of AT THE PIG'S.
explanation.definitionFit: Long thin pasta is a food you could eat.

clue.text: They speak of detective writer

explanation.surface: Talkers discussing a crime novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: Dorothy L Sayers wrote the Lord Peter Wimsey detective novels.
explanation.definitionFit: People who utter words are speakers, and Dorothy L Sayers was a crime novelist.

clue.text: On Tuesday paramour returns with charge greatly changed

indicators.note: returns says the pieces before it come back the other way

parts.note: a paramour is a lover
an ionised particle carries an electric charge

explanation.surface: A Tuesday tryst where the lover comes back charged and transformed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns TU and LOVER together into REVOLUT; IONISED (charged, like an ion) follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To transform something fundamentally is to bring about radical change in it.

clue.text: Is in power, we hear, having the means of control

indicators.note: we hear says the previous words are to be judged by their sound

parts.note: a monarch who reigns holds power

explanation.surface: A ruler who holds the means of control.
explanation.walkthrough: REIGNS sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Straps a rider uses to steer a horse are the means of control; also used figuratively, as in the reins of government.

clue.text: Letter writer reveals something unknown by a railway

parts.note: a secret is something not known

explanation.surface: A correspondent discloses a mystery found beside a railway line.
explanation.definitionFit: An office assistant handles correspondence and types letters.

clue.text: Some text remember ate could be far from moderate

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some reading-matter recalls an immoderate eater.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'ate could be far from moderate' as the definition, but only 'far from moderate' defines the answer; 'ate could be' is padding in the clue as held.
explanation.definitionFit: Something very far from moderation is at the utmost limit, intense or radical.

clue.text: One, not that woman?

parts.note: a means one
taken as written
her refers to a woman already mentioned

explanation.surface: Asking for a different one, not her.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also works as the definition: a different one rather than that particular woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Another means an additional or different one, not the one already meant.

clue.text: The cost to the Light Brigade?

definitions.text: The cost to the Light Brigade?

parts.words: The cost to the Light Brigade?
parts.note: the Charge of the Light Brigade was a famous cavalry attack, and the bill run up is the cost charged to it

explanation.surface: A question about what the Light Brigade's doomed attack cost.
explanation.walkthrough: The Charge of the Light Brigade (Balaclava, 1854) suggests an account of that charge; read as shopping, it is a store credit arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A credit arrangement with a shop lets purchases be billed later.

clue.text: Almost look up to a lieutenant with unknown naval power

indicators.note: almost means the word for look up to stops one letter short

parts.note: to admire someone is to look up to them
y is one of the letters algebra uses for an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: Nearly revering a young officer in the navy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' drops the last letter of ADMIRE, leaving ADMIR. The Admiralty was the British body governing the Royal Navy.
explanation.definitionFit: The British navy's governing department held command of the fleet, its sea strength.

clue.text: Intermediaries taking a long time with new French companies

parts.note: an age is a long time, as in waiting for ages
Cie is the French abbreviation for compagnie, so the plural is Cies

explanation.surface: Go-betweens taking ages with fresh French firms.
explanation.definitionFit: Agencies act on behalf of others as go-betweens.

clue.text: Reflective tabloid journalism?

parts.note: the Mirror is a British tabloid newspaper
journalism is a form of writing

explanation.surface: Thoughtful reporting in a popular newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Daily Mirror is a British tabloid. 'Reflective' means not thoughtful but reversed, as in a mirror.
explanation.definitionFit: Script written backwards reads normally only when reflected in a looking-glass.

clue.text: No buts when you do this

definitions.text: No buts when you do this

parts.words: No buts when you do this
parts.note: a carpenter's butt joint meets edge to edge; when pieces instead extend over each other there is no butting

explanation.surface: An instruction that leaves no room for objections.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buts' sounds like butts, the edge-to-edge joints; extending one piece over another means they no longer meet end to end.
explanation.definitionFit: When two things extend over each other they do not merely meet end-on.

clue.text: House or castle?

explanation.surface: Asking whether a royal residence is a house or a castle.
explanation.walkthrough: Both senses: the House of Windsor is the British royal family, and Windsor Castle is its residence west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: The British royal dynasty takes the name of the Berkshire castle that is a royal residence.

clue.text: Provide wherewithal to make a fellow cross

parts.note: a ford is a place to cross a river; to ford is to cross

explanation.surface: Finding the money to let a man get across.
explanation.definitionFit: To afford can mean to give or supply, as in a view affording pleasure.

clue.text: Pine, perhaps, to have fine Irish ancestry?

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
a family tree charts ancestry

explanation.surface: Longing to have a good Irish pedigree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pine' looks like the verb to long for; it is the conifer.
explanation.definitionFit: The pine is one kind of conifer; the definition gives an example.

clue.text: Grandma's sharp to get this cloth

parts.note: nan is an informal word for grandmother
keen means sharp, as in a keen blade

explanation.surface: Granny's eager to get hold of some fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Nankeen is a yellowish cotton fabric originally from Nanjing.

clue.text: No longer having drinks outdoors?

parts.note: ex means former, no longer what it was
It is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and It

explanation.surface: Giving up drinks on the terrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outdoors' is split as out doors: ways out. Gin and It (Italian vermouth) is an old British cocktail.
explanation.definitionFit: Doors leading outside are ways out of a building.

clue.text: Perhaps olives growing here could be great sources of wealth?

definitions.text: Perhaps olives growing here could be great sources of wealth?

parts.words: Perhaps olives growing here could be great sources of wealth?
parts.note: olives yield oil, so land where they grow could be called by an oil name, while the real places are petroleum reserves that bring riches

explanation.surface: Musing that an olive grove might make someone rich.
explanation.walkthrough: The olive grove picture is false: the real answer is land that yields petroleum.
explanation.definitionFit: Areas rich in petroleum deposits are major sources of national wealth.

clue.text: Genre of second Kipling poem in Channel Islands

indicators.note: in puts the poem inside the islands' abbreviation

parts.note: If is a famous poem by Rudyard Kipling

explanation.surface: A second Kipling poem set in Jersey or Guernsey makes a literary genre.
explanation.definitionFit: Science fiction is a literary and film genre.

clue.text: Times to stun it's said

indicators.note: it's said says the previous word is to be judged by how it sounds

parts.note: to daze someone is to stun them

explanation.surface: A remark about stunning times.
explanation.walkthrough: DAZE sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Days are periods, as in the old days meaning past times.

clue.text: Dior's past being worried by such takers-off

indicators.note: being worried, like a dog worrying a bone, means the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Dior's history being mocked by impersonators.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being worried' rearranges DIORSPAST.
explanation.definitionFit: Takers-off are mimics, and parodists imitate others for comic effect.
